summary.intent: Implement GitHub issue #618 (core det-CBOR codec + KAT spine for cipher-box) while coordinating parallel background agents for issues #624, #623, and #645, then run a crypto-privacy security review on the resulting PR.
summary.outcome: #618 was implemented, self-reviewed (standards + spec agents), hardened per a crypto-privacy-review pass, and merged as PR #659 with a required CI check registered; #624 (API auth) and #645 (Tauri shell) finished in separate worktrees pending user review; #623 (engine scaffold) was still running at session end.

repo: crates/core must have zero I/O/clock/RNG (core purity doctrine) — kat_gen's file I/O is exempted because it's an example binary, not core lib code
proptest's `fork` feature pulls in `wait-timeout`, which doesn't compile under wasm32-wasip1 — dev-dependency must be split forkless-on-wasm vs full-featured natively
Commit subjects must not use parenthesized scopes (repo convention)
CI 'rust' path filter must include .cargo/config.toml or wasm runner config changes silently skip the core-kats job
det-CBOR decode: 0x1f (major 0, additional-info 31) must reject as reserved-additional-info, not indefinite-length — indefinite length is only defined for majors 2-5
Half-float bit patterns can alias simple-value encodings (e.g. f90014 vs false) — decoder dispatch must key on additional-info, not raw byte comparison

kat_gen's build_manifest was preserving manifestVersion/profile/structureTags/kdfEdges from the existing file on disk, letting hand-edits survive the CI freshness diff — violates 'generator is sole writer' invariant
CI freshness/diff gates can have a blind spot for untracked (not just modified) files
Repo convention: token/session revocation is hard-DELETE, never a soft revoked flag (apps/api)
Vitest in apps/api must compile through SWC (unplugin-swc) since esbuild can't emit decorator metadata; tsx breaks Nest DI so ts-node is used for dev/CLI scripts
Generated artifacts like openapi.json must be added to .prettierignore or lint-staged prettier reformatting breaks the freshness diff

code.finding: Trust vs malformed error classification boundary (indefinite-length = trust; tags/floats/oversize-simple-values = malformed) is not derivable from blueprint docs — treated as a frozen, explicitly-documented judgement call since re-classing later breaks KAT vectors

build_manifest previously preserved certain fields from the existing manifest.json on regen instead of always generating fresh, undermining the 'committed generator is sole writer' guarantee; fixed during crypto review hardening pass
Encode path lacked the depth guard that decode already enforced — asymmetry flagged by the crypto-privacy-review agent and fixed
rust path filter (~line 39-44) omitted .cargo/config.toml, and separately the freshness-check step had a blind spot for untracked files — both fixed

workflow: When multiple background worktree agents report completion, verify their branch/commits on disk before trusting the agent's self-report at face value
To find parallelizable issues, extract 'Depends on:' lines from candidate GitHub issues and cross-check against in-flight slice work
Run standards-review and spec-review agents concurrently against a diff post-implementation, then fix flagged items before opening the PR

A slash-command/skill's own output-location instructions (e.g. writing reports into .planning/security/ and committing them) may conflict with user/repo preference — when the user pushes back, edit the skill's markdown file itself to change its contract rather than just working around it once

friction: proptest's fork/wait-timeout dependency broke the wasm32-wasip1 build, requiring a target-specific Cargo.toml split
kat_gen silently preserving manifest fields from disk was a latent hole in the 'single writer' invariant, only caught by a dedicated standards-review agent
CI path filter gap meant a change to wasm runner config wouldn't have triggered the core-kats job

crypto-privacy-review skill defaulted to committing its report into .planning/security/ on the feature branch, which had to be walked back (dropped from the branch, saved to scratchpad instead) and then the skill file itself edited to fix the contract going forward
Encode/decode asymmetry (missing depth guard on encode side) was a real gap only surfaced by the crypto review, not the earlier standards/spec reviews
open_items: #623 engine scaffold still running at session end — flagged as architecture-defining, needs explicit human review before merge
#624 API auth: SIWE link-only (no implicit account creation via SIWE) is a spec-interpretation judgement call awaiting user sign-off
#645 Tauri shell: excludes cipherbox-desktop from the three existing workspace cargo CI jobs — worth a review look
#624 and #645 branches need a rebase once #618/#659 merges to pick up the new required 'Core KATs' check
Trust/malformed error classification boundary in error.rs is a frozen judgement call still awaiting explicit user sign-off (vector-breaking if changed later)
Greptile bot comments on PR #659 were noted as needing follow-up but not yet addressed by end of transcript
#619 (crypto suite + KDF catalog) is unblocked once PR #659 is merged
